title: The Lunar New Year Effect on Stock Market Returns and Volatility: Evidence from Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange
content: This study is devoted to investigating the Lunar New Year effect on market returns and volatility for Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE). The data employed in this study is a daily series of the VN30-Index, which is a market capitalization weighted index of 30 large capitalization and high liquidity stocks traded on the HOSE, for the period from February 6, 2012 to December 31, 2024. The empirical findings derived ordinary least square (OLS), exponential generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity [EGARCH(1,1)] regression models consistently confirm that the average return in the last two days and five days before the Lunar New Year are significantly higher than the average market returns on other days of the year. However, this study finds that the average return during the first two trading days and five trading days following the Lunar New Year are not significantly different from the average market returns on other days throughout the year. Regarding the Lunar New Year effect on the market volatility, the results obtained from the EGARCH(1,1) model reveal that the Lunar New Year effect on the market volatility is not present for the HOSE.
